messages.subject: Problem with log transformed variables
parts:
Dear lavaan members, 
I am running a study fixed effects models which includes 7000 cases approx across 20 studies. I am getting the following error/warning message which I am unable to trace and resolve. The model works fine without transforming the data. Could you please assist? thanks so much!. Borja
The model does not converge:

Error in validObject(.Object) : 
  invalid class “Fit” object: invalid object for slot "fx.group" in class "Fit": got class "NULL", should be or extend class "numeric"
In addition: Warning message:
In lav_model_estimate(lavmodel = lavmodel, lavpartable = lavpartable,  :
  lavaan WARNING: the optimizer warns that a solution has NOT been found!


when I try the model without dividing CRF by 10, the message changes to:

Warning messages:
1: In lav_data_full(data = data, group = group, cluster = cluster,  :
  lavaan WARNING: some observed variances are (at least) a factor 1000 times larger than others; use varTable(fit) to investigate
2: In lav_model_estimate(lavmodel = lavmodel, lavpartable = lavpartable,  :
  lavaan WARNING: the optimizer warns that a solution has NOT been found!

Here is my model syntax:

Cors <- expand.grid(paste0("study_", 2:length(dums)), paste0("study_", 2:length(dums))) %>%
  filter(Var1 != Var2)

Cors <- Cors[!duplicated(t(apply(Cors, 1, sort))), ] %>%
  mutate(Cor = paste(Var1, "~~", Var2) )


m <- mean(IDA_data_filter_dum$crf_1, na.rm=TRUE)
s <-sd(IDA_data_filter_dum$crf_1, na.rm=TRUE)
names(IDA_data_filter_dum)

### I am transforming the physical activity variables (they are highly skewed). I am also, to avoid problems with variance, dividing crf by 10. 

IDA_data_filter_dum$vig_1log<-log(IDA_data_filter_dum$vig_1 +1)
IDA_data_filter_dum$vig_2log<-log(IDA_data_filter_dum$vig_2  +1)
IDA_data_filter_dum$mpa_1log<-log(IDA_data_filter_dum$mpa_1  +1)
IDA_data_filter_dum$mpa_2log<-log(IDA_data_filter_dum$mpa_1  +1)
IDA_data_filter_dum$crf_1_10<-IDA_data_filter_dum$crf_1/10
IDA_data_filter_dum$crf_2_10<-IDA_data_filter_dum$crf_2/10


Mod <- '
crf_2_10 ~ crf_1_10 + treat + vig_1log + mpa_1log + bmi_z + age_z + sex
vig_2log ~ crf_1_10 + treat + vig_1log + mpa_1log + bmi_z + age_z + sex
mpa_2log ~ crf_1_10 + treat + vig_1log + mpa_1log + bmi_z + age_z + sex

 
crf_1_10 ~~ vig_1log + mpa_1log + treat + bmi_z + age_z + sex
vig_1log ~~ mpa_1log  + treat + bmi_z + age_z + sex
mpa_1log ~~ treat + bmi_z + age_z + sex
treat ~~ bmi_z + age_z + sex
bmi_z ~~  age_z + sex
age_z ~~ sex

crf_2_10 ~~ vig_2log + mpa_2log
vig_2log ~~ mpa_2log
 
DO(2,20,1)
study_% ~~ crf_1_10 + vig_1log + mpa_1log + bmi_z + age_z + sex
crf_2_10  ~ study_%
vig_2log  ~ study_%
mpa_2log  ~ study_%
study_% ~~ treat
DOEND
'  %>% doparse

Mod <- paste(Mod, " ",Cors$Cor %>% paste(collapse = " "), collapse = " ")


Mod_fit <- sem(Mod, IDA_data_filter_dum,  missing = "fiml")

summary(Mod_fit, standardized = TRUE, fit.measures = TRUE)

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Problem with log transformed variables
parts:
Most of us only speak native R, not the language that Hadley Wickham wishes R was, so it is not entirely clear what you are trying to do with those tidyverse pipes.  The DO loop within the lavaan model syntax appears to automate the addition of 19 dummy codes.  Try using cat() to print your lavaan syntax, not only to check that it did what you expected, but so you can copy/paste that into the message for readers here to understand what model you are trying to fit. 

Adding so many dummy codes increases the size of your covariance matrix.  You could try setting conditional.x=TRUE to partial out the exogenous effects, so that your model is fitted to the residual covariance matrix (computationally advantageous).  Even if you don't do this, you don't have to specify exogenous (co)variances in your lavaan model syntax when you are using the default fixed.x=TRUE.  Just let the sample statistics be treated as fixed.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Problem with log transformed variables
parts: it is interesting that the model works fine with non-transformed variables but it does not work when I log transform the variables

Indeed, a monotonic transformation should not cause such a problem, unless something is not going as expected.  Have you looked carefully at your transformed data?  Try inspecting histograms, counting missing data to make sure that adding 1 was sufficient to prevent "NaN" or "-Inf" values resulting from taking the log of negative or zero, respectively.  Also scatterplots of an original variable by its transformation.  Some exploration might reveal whether anything unexpected happened during transformation.

All that being said, I wouldn't recommend log-transforming your data anyway.  There are existing robust corrections for non-normal data (see the estimator, se, and test arguments in the ?lavOptions help page).

Good luck,

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen
